page: Microsoft Azure E8-2ads_v5 is an EADSv5-family virtual machine running on the Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor. It features an AMD EPYC 7763 processor with an x86_64 architecture, providing 2 dedicated vCPUs mapped to 1 physical core with 2 threads. The CPU operates at a clock speed of 3.525 GHz and includes 32 MB of L3 cache. The instance is equipped with 64.0 GB of RAM, representing a high memory-to-vCPU ratio of 32 GB per vCPU. It also includes 307 GB of local SSD storage and is Premium Storage capable, with no bundled GPUs.

Benchmark data reveals a clear performance asymmetry. The single-core CPU performance is strong, ranking in the top 25% in stress-ng tests, and single-threaded tasks like gzip compression and bzip3 decompression show average performance. However, due to the low core count of 1 physical core, multi-core benchmarks are weak, with stress-ng multi-core and Geekbench multi-core scores falling into the bottom 25% and bottom 10% respectively. Memory bandwidth is also constrained, with read-only small block cached bandwidth scoring in the bottom 10% and large block write bandwidth in the bottom 25%.

This server is designed for memory-intensive workloads that do not require high parallel processing power. The high RAM density relative to the low vCPU count provides qualitative cost efficiency for applications that are memory-bound rather than compute-bound, avoiding the need to provision excess vCPUs just to acquire sufficient memory. Appropriate workloads include small-scale in-memory databases, caching layers, lightweight text processing, and basic web serving where memory capacity is the primary constraint.
